english.sense: The introductory chapter that gathers the foundational topics and prerequisites for the model-theory material.

openlogic_locator.role: English chapter title and bounded introductory scope

isv.inflection_use_note: Osnovy is the nominative plural of feminine osnova ‘basis, base’; teorije is genitive singular of teorija, and modelov is genitive plural of model. Use Osnovy teorije modelov as the chapter title.

ru.note: The pinned Russian column converges on the osnova/baza family; this supports intelligibility, not national-standard certification.

uk.note: The pinned Ukrainian column supplies the same core osnova family with podstava support; this supports intelligibility, not national-standard certification.

pl.note: The pinned Polish column confirms the shared basis/base sense through podstawa and baza.

cs.note: The pinned Czech column supplies the corresponding základ family; this is a cross-Slavic comparandum, not a claim that Czech spelling is the Interslavic head.

bcs.note: The pinned Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian-facing column contains osnova alongside baza and temelj, giving the strongest direct South-Slavic support.

bg.note: The pinned Bulgarian column confirms основа/база and makes the chosen root readily legible in Cyrillic.

official_isv_evidence.claim_boundary: Fixes the English Open Logic chapter title and scope; it does not certify an Interslavic lexical choice.
Pins the live published dictionary head osnova and its basis/base sense; it is not represented as an immutable official release.
Provides the direct basic/fundamental adjective as a semantic cross-check for the chapter-title sense.
Supports regular plural and genitive morphology used in the title, not specialist lexical certification.

official_isv_evidence.locator: standard Latin alphabet and Cyrillic equivalence sections
official_isv_evidence.claim_boundary: Supports the recorded Latin/Cyrillic spelling, not the editorial choice among synonyms.
Supports deterministic Cyrillic projection only; it does not select the Latin term.

rationale: Osnova is the directly pinned Interslavic basis/base noun, and its nominative plural osnovy is the natural chapter-heading form for foundational material. Teorije modelov reuses the already accepted model-theory inflection, yielding a transparent title across Slavic readers.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Bazis is intelligible in some Slavic usage but is not the pinned basic-dictionary head for the general basis/base sense and narrows the pan-Slavic root convergence.

evidence_locators.role: Selected osnova head over a less-supported bazis alternative

rejected_alternatives.reason: Fundamenty foregrounds a physical foundation and is less suitable for an introductory chapter whose contents are conceptual prerequisites and definitions.

confidence.basis: Direct dictionary head, transparent plural morphology, accepted model/theory components, and broad cross-Slavic comparanda.

source_units.locator: standard Latin alphabet and Cyrillic equivalence sections

revision_lineage.change_note: Initial bounded terminology selection for the OLP-0183 model-theory basics wrapper.
revision_lineage.authority_boundary: Open Logic edition preference; no official or native certification claimed

uncertainties: The title is an editorial chapter-heading choice; future corpus context may distinguish osnovy from more specialized foundational terminology.
